author: DTrim99
body:
Good catch on the outcome, and the root cause turns out to sit one line higher on the K-40: PolicyEngine's tax before credits (137.65 = 3.1% × 4,440) is what's wrong, not the EITC machinery. Kansas's zero-liability rule (K.S.A. 79-32,110; visible directly in the 2021 tax table, where the married-joint column is 0 up to $5,000 of taxable income) zeroes line 8 on this return — taxable income 4,441 — and with line 16 = 0 the page 8 worksheet routes the entire Kansas EITC to line 25 as refundable, exactly as TaxAct shows (121 refund, with the $250 food sales credit unusable).

PolicyEngine has the $5,000/$2,500 zero-tax thresholds parameterized, but the formula tests them against Kansas AGI (18,341 here) rather than taxable income, so the rule almost never fires. With that fixed, our tax goes to 0 and the existing EITC split logic (which follows the worksheet: nonrefundable up to line 16, remainder refundable) automatically produces siitax = −120.69 vs your −121 (rounding of the federal 709.95 → 710). Filed PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9172 with a fix.

Example household:
```
taxsimid,year,state,mstat,page,sage,depx,pwages,intrec,gssi,idtl
4337417,2021,17,2,72,80,0,17809.523,530.6839,44865.844,5
```
